static_traits.name: Lin Jie
static_traits.social_status: Having a few friends to talk about average topics with, but not yet discussing gardening-related inferiority with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before; has not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, high cooperativeness; able to identify and describe automatic thoughts and negative patterns; slightly nervous tone but positive attitude, with a strong sense of hope

basic_info.main_problem: I am stuck in a sense of inadequacy and low self-esteem regarding gardening skills. I constantly feel I am the worst gardener and will never improve. Every time I work in the garden, self-criticism and negative thinking arise, leading to dread and a sense of failure.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of inadequacy and self-doubt are affecting my overall well-being and enjoyment of the hobby.

special_situations.event: After planting new flowers last week, most withered within a few days
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If one attempt fails, it means I have no ability, and I will not succeed in the future either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Compensating for the 'sense of incompetence' by reading gardening books and trying new methods, while reducing willingness to get back to the garden
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Why keep trying? I will never be good at gardening

special_situations.event: Every time entering the garden to start working
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only a perfect result counts as success; otherwise it is failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids or reduces gardening activities to avoid feeling like a failure again

special_situations.event: Thinking that others might see my garden or judge my gardening
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: My worth depends on the views of others; if they see my failure, they will look down on me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding talking about gardening frustrations with friends; trying not to let others see the garden
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am awful / will mock me

special_situations.event: Recalls the herbs successfully planted and thriving last month
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: A single success is just luck; it cannot change my overall incompetence
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring and downplaying positive evidence; continuing to reinforce negative self-labels
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is not real success, just good luck

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a capable gardener, able to confidently enjoy the pleasure of gardening
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure being negated and mocked by others; fearing exposing the 'not good enough' self
defense_goal: Reducing the hurt of external negation through self-criticism and preemptive negation
Reduces discussing gardening distress with others, avoids being seen to maintain a sense of security

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about letting others see her garden or suggesting she seek help from others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others may look down on me like judges; exposure will bring shame
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First normalizing shame and defenses; gentle, steady tone; using open-ended questioning to invite specifying the sources of worry, gradually exploring the tolerable range of 'being seen', and offering safe boundary options.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes my successful experiences (such as successfully growing herbs) and gives affirmation
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Positive feedback is not reliable; success is just luck and cannot prove I am capable
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First empathizing with her caution and uncertainty, slowing speech pace; then gently confronting, guiding to distinguish 'evidence' from 'interpretation', inviting review of concrete behaviors and outcomes, helping her acknowledge the validity of partial successes.

manifestations: Gardening changed from a beloved hobby into a source of stress and a symbol of failure
Experiences difficulty and failure feelings when working in the garden
Although having friends to talk to, not yet discussing gardening-related inadequacy and shame with them
Worrying about others' opinions leads to self-isolation
outcomes: Lacking real support and corrective experiences

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the behavioral impulses they want to direct at others or the outside world and instead does it to themselves, turning energy from outward to inward.
manifestations: Having friends to talk to yet not expressing gardening-related inadequacy and shame
Bearing self-criticism and frustration alone; not actively seeking support

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others.
manifestations: Worrying others will look down on oneself or mock one's garden
Externally attributes self-shame to 'others will evaluate negatively'

contact_model.definition: Has poor self-reflection and excessive self-restriction, harsh self-reproach, overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Overly cautious before starting gardening, presetting failure scenarios

exception_events.target_problem: When actually gardening, Lin Jie usually engages in self-denial, anticipates failure, and develops dread, thereby reducing investment and enjoyment.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last month successfully planted several herbs that are thriving; felt proud and accomplished at the time, briefly recognizing her own ability (e.g. 'maybe I am not entirely terrible').
exception_events.reason: Clue: during that planting, the client maintained continuous care and observation and followed the operating steps, focusing more on the process rather than self-judgment, so a better outcome and experience emerged.

positive_force: Positive attitude, willing to try behavioral experiments
Having had successful experience (herbs thriving), which can form corrective evidence
Proactively learns (reading gardening books and methods)
Has some social support potential (has friends to communicate with)
negative_force: Negating positive results; labeling and intense self-criticism
Predicting failure and personalization, excessively concerned about others' evaluations
Developing dread and avoidance in gardening situations; reduced investment; impaired self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-denial and dread appearing in gardening activities, accompanied by avoiding practice
antecedent: When starting to work in the garden
Seeing newly planted flowers wither within days
Thinking that others might see and evaluate one's garden
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralizing one or several failures into overall inadequate ability, and making others' evaluations the core of self-worth, forming catastrophic and prophetic thinking.
target_behavior.function: Avoids failure and shame, avoiding negative evaluation by others and self-exposure.
target_behavior.consequence: Gardening enjoyment markedly declining; low mood and impaired self-esteem; reduced gardening practice and investment.
